coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy Z2 only—45–55 minutes, sub-130 avg HR. Your resting HR is elevated 7.5 bpm above 30-day average and recovery score sits at 46/100 (moderate), which means your nervous system is still clearing load from peak phase. You ran hard yesterday (11.82 mi @ 130 bpm) and the day before (6.41 mi @ 123 bpm). Monday in taper is not a day to test fitness. Keep the effort conversational, focus on movement quality, and treat this as active recovery. Alpine terrain demands leg resilience, not accumulated fatigue.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: You're 25 days out from race day and your sleep efficiency dropped to 70%—below your 30-day average of ~82%. This often signals poor glycogen repletion or inadequate post-run carbs. After today's easy run, consume 1.0–1.2g carbs per kg body weight within 90 minutes (e.g., rice + protein + fruit). At night, prioritize carbs and electrolytes 2–3 hours before bed; aim for 8+ hours sleep to drop that resting HR back toward 66. During taper, nutrition becomes your sharpening tool—don't under-fuel thinking you need to cut weight.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Eight hours is sufficient volume, but 70% efficiency is a yellow flag. Elevated resting HR + moderate recovery score suggests incomplete parasympathetic reset. Tonight: no screens after 21:30, cool room (60–65°F ideally), and consider a 15-minute walk or 5-minute mobility flow to lower cortisol. You're traveling constantly for work—guard sleep as fiercely as you guard your long runs. The Julian Alps 50K will test mental resilience at altitude; that starts with deep, unbroken sleep now.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: Taper anxiety is real at week 4-out, especially when recovery metrics look soft. Resist the urge to prove fitness with a hard workout. Your recent runs show you're capable (130 bpm sustained over 11+ miles)—trust that. Use these next 25 days to *refine* pacing strategy on the actual Julian Alps terrain, manage work stress (your biggest variable), and arrive fresh. The race is won by athletes who taper smart and arrive confident, not by those who panic-train into overreach.
